scope: one-run visible-byte preparation before any model execution

synthetic_arm_checks.source: fixture._fixture compiled schedule and preflight release per arm

negative_controls: changed prompt or extra release entry rejected before stage creation
release prompt changed after visible inspection rejected before stage manifest
valid case ZIP temporarily substituted during extraction and then restored rejected
extracted case file altered after extraction rejected
nested extracted case file altered after extraction rejected
work directory replaced by outside symlink rejected
failure after pending manifest write leaves no stage.json
caller-owned calendar mutated during pending write cannot alter stage limits
existing destination preserved and relative destination rejected

initial_false_successes: temporary valid case ZIP substitution yielded a success manifest with different case bytes
case mutation and work symlink yielded a success manifest
an error after direct stage.json write left a valid-looking success marker
caller mutated per_run_limits from 23 to 24 after release verification and stage.json published 24 with the original schedule SHA
independent_review.reviewer: native read-only development agent, not an independent human custodian

limitations: The source schedule, run, case, and review are synthetic and unsealed; no reserved case was opened.
The local actual toolkit ZIP is ignored by Git and has no external custody.
Staging does not install T, run a model, mount isolated roots, enforce policy or budgets, or authenticate provider receipts.
A same-UID writer can still race point-in-time checks after the last verification; a future executor must revalidate and use isolation and custody.
The final stage.json rename is the last operation on normal return; host-crash durability of the rename was not proven.
